## Purpose
Awesome DeepSeek Agent is a documentation-only curated catalog for configuring DeepSeek models in third-party AI agents and coding assistants. It contains no application runtime, service implementation, or build pipeline.

## Entry Points and Navigation
`README.md` is the English catalog entry point: it introduces the collection, links each supported tool guide, and points users to DeepSeek account/API resources. `README.zh-CN.md` is its Chinese counterpart. Each table entry routes users into a guide under `docs/`.

Paths: `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `docs/`

## Guide Content Layer
One Markdown document per supported integration is the repository’s primary unit of content. Guides are organized by external product rather than by shared implementation, covering installation, DeepSeek provider/model configuration, and initial usage.

Paths: `docs/claude_code.md`, `docs/codex.md`, `docs/openclaw.md`

## Bilingual Documentation Boundary
Most guides have parallel English and Simplified Chinese versions. Changes to a guide should generally preserve this paired structure and update the catalog links/descriptions when a tool is added or materially renamed.

Paths: `docs/astrbot.md`, `docs/astrbot.zh-CN.md`, `docs/deepseek-tui.md`

## External Integration Boundary
The repository documents integrations but does not own them. Its material external dependencies are DeepSeek’s platform/API and the independently maintained agent clients, IDE extensions, desktop apps, terminal tools, and chat-platform agents described by each guide. Authentication and model access occur in users’ local tool configurations, outside this repository.

Paths: `README.md`, `docs/cline.md`, `docs/github_copilot.md`

## Content Contribution Flow
Contribution policy is centralized in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; contributors add or revise a tool-specific guide, maintain language variants where applicable, and register the guide in the README catalog. The pull-request template standardizes review-facing contribution metadata.

Paths: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `README.md`

## Assets and Supporting References
Shared documentation assets reside under `docs/assets/`. The docs also include dedicated setup guides for a broad range of supported clients, from terminal coding agents to multi-channel assistant platforms; these are independent content endpoints rather than executable modules.

Paths: `docs/assets`, `docs/reasonix.md`, `docs/lobehub.md`
